# Approximate Bayesian Computation

The focus of the miniproject [on $N_e$ inferences from AFS](project-afs.html)
was on using simulations performed across a grid of values of parameters of
interest, computing a summary statistic (such as AFS) on each simulation
outcome, and the picking the parameter value which resulted in a simulation
closest to the equivalent summary statistic observed in real data.

Approximate Bayesian Computation (ABC) is a technique which works very similarly
with one important exception. Rather than simulation from discrete values of a
parameter grid, simulation parameters are drawn from continuous prior
distributions, and simulated summary statistics are matched using more elaborate
mathematical comparisons against empirical statistics to produce posterior
distributions of parameter values.

In this miniproject, you can learn how to use the [R package
_demografr_](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2025.12.18.694482v1),
which is a companion framework to _slendr_, to construct ABC inference pipeline
to estimate the values of parameters of interest for a model which you'd like to
study. Having done this entire workshop, you know all there's to know about
_slendr_ modeling and simulations, giving you a huge head start. I suggest you
start by taking a look at the paper linked above, using it as a tutorial, and
then continue working on your own.
